meta.note: Trimmed 2026-08-30 to the two currencies the backend actually quotes. It held nine (USD EUR GBP INR AED SAR JPY AUD CAD), verified against the API on 2026-08-14, but the backend has since withdrawn seven and now answers {"INR":"88","USD":"1"}. These are CHARGING rates, not display-only: checkout sends the on-screen currency, so a table richer than the backend's does not offer more choice, it quotes prices the backend will not honour. That is what put 'Prices are shown in EUR, but this order is charged in USD' on the payment page. Restoring a currency here means restoring it on the BACKEND first and then running `npm run catalog`; adding a row by hand re-creates the same mismatch. fx.current_rates() and fx.latest_rate() both resolve through latest_rate, so a stored FxRate row beats settings.FX_RATES in both.
